headline: Pope Francis kept a diary for 32 years. Now it's a book.
summary: The Vatican published excerpts on Tuesday. Francis wrote in a leather-bound calendar from 1992, when he was a bishop in Buenos Aires, to August 2024. He describes seeing the devil three times and a crisis in 2021-22 over his urge to run everything alone. Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, who edited it, says Francis wanted it published.

cover_question.q: Did the Pope really see the devil?

cover_answer: He wrote that he did. Three times.
table_question: Would you want your private diary read after you're gone?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Pope Francis, who led the Catholic Church, kept a diary for 32 years. He wanted people to read it, and now it is a book. A diary is like a box where you keep your thoughts, even the scary ones. He wrote his scary ones down, and he got through them. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A diary is a box for thoughts. The devil stays on the page.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and here that feature is the devil, so the script never says the word unless the child does. The anchor is the diary as a box for thoughts, a thing they own. Expect 'is the devil real?' Francis believed so. People believe different things. You are safe at home either way.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Pope Francis kept a diary from 1992 to 2024, and now it is a book. He describes seeing the devil three times, and two years when he felt he had to run everything alone. A diary works like a coach's notebook: write the mistakes down so you can see them. His last two books came out of that stretch.
8-12.why: Wrote it down, saw it, wrote his way out. The chain is the story.
8-12.why_long: At 12 a child is working out cause and effect, and this story is a chain they can hold: a bad stretch, written down for two years, then two books that came out of it. The coach's notebook is the mechanism, mistakes on paper so you can see them. Expect 'did he really see the devil?' He wrote that he did, three times. The rest is theirs.

13-17.script: Should a private diary be published after the writer dies? Francis kept his for 32 years and wanted it out, his editor says. He writes of shame and two years of feeling he had to run everything alone. Second: in 2018 he dismissed abuse victims in Chile, then wrote of "the entrance to hell." Does that count?
13-17.why: Two true things: he was wrong about Chile, and he wrote that down.
13-17.why_long: At 15 they can hold two true things at once: the most powerful Catholic alive doubted himself for two years, and he wanted the record printed. The script hands them Chile, where he was wrong and wrote so. Expect 'did he ever say sorry?' The article says he ordered an inquiry and found the victims were right. The diary adds how it felt.

5-7.a: Pope Francis believed so. People believe different things about that. You are safe at home either way.

8-12.q: Did the Pope really see the devil?
8-12.a: He wrote that he did, three times. What it was is your call.

8-12.q: Why would a pope have a crisis?
8-12.a: Bad pain, a Vatican money scandal, and feeling he alone had to fix it all.

13-17.a: The cardinal who edited it says Francis wanted it published.

13-17.q: Did he ever say sorry for Chile?
13-17.a: He ordered an inquiry and found the victims were right.
